note.text:
A quadratic equation has x² as its highest power: x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
• Make one side zero.
• Factorise the other side: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0.
• If a product is zero, one of the factors is zero: x − 2 = 0 or x − 3 = 0.
• So x = 2 or x = 3. A quadratic usually has two solutions (roots).
• x² = 5x: do not divide by x (you would lose x = 0). Write x² − 5x = 0, x(x − 5) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 5.
• Check each root in the original equation.

sections.heading: The zero product rule
sections.text:
If two numbers multiply to give zero, at least one of them is zero. ({3} × {0} = {0}; but {3} × {2} is never {0}.)
So if (x − {2})(x − {3}) = {0}, either x − {2} = {0} or x − {3} = {0}. That gives x = {2} or x = {3}.
This only works with zero. If (x − {2})(x − {3}) = {6}, you cannot say x − {2} = {6}: first expand, make one side zero, and factorise again.

sections.heading: The method
sections.text:
Solve x² + {mono(2, 'x')} = {15}.
• Make one side zero: {poly([1, 'x²'], [2, 'x'], [-15, ''])} = {0}.
• Factorise: {'(' + poly([1, 'x'], [5, '']) + ')' + '(' + poly([1, 'x'], [-3, '']) + ')'} = {0}.
• Each factor zero: x = {-5} or x = {3}.
• Check: ({3})² + {2} × {3} = {15}. ✓ and ({-5})² + {2} × ({-5}) = {15}. ✓
Notice the sign change: the bracket (x + {5}) gives the root x = {-5}.

sections.heading: Roots that make sense
sections.text:
In real problems, a quadratic may give one root that cannot be right, such as a negative length or a fraction of a person. State both roots, then reject the impossible one with a reason: "x = {-8} is rejected because a width cannot be negative."
And remember: never divide both sides by x. In x² = {mono(6, 'x')}, factorise x(x − {6}) = {0}: the roots are {0} and {6}.

Either x − {p} = {0}, so x = {p}; or x + {-q} = {0}, so x = {q}.

misconceptions.explain: x − {br(max(p, q))} = {0} gives x = {max(p, q)}: watch the sign.

solution: x = {p} or x = {q}. The larger is {answer}.

questions.prompt: Solve {poly([a, 'x²'], [a * n + m, 'x'], [m * n, ''])} = {0}. One root is a whole number: give it.

misconceptions.explain: {mono(a, 'x')} + {m} = {0} gives x = {-m} ÷ {a}, not a whole number.

questions.prompt: A rectangular plot in Bamenda is {k} m longer than it is wide. Its area is {w * (w + k)} m². Find its width in metres.

misconceptions.explain: A width cannot be negative: reject x = {-(w + k)}.
{w + k} m is the length; the question asks for the width.

solution: Let the width be x m: x(x + {k}) = {w * (w + k)}.
x = {w} or x = {-(w + k)}. A width cannot be negative, so the width is {answer} m.
